title: Sell Mineral Rights in Idamay, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Idamay, WV
metaDescription: Idamay, Marion County mineral owners: small fractional interests from coal-camp era severances, near legacy Big Injun wells and the Marcellus corridor.
heroLead: Idamay is a small unincorporated community in Marion County where mineral interests trace to the same coal-camp era severances that shaped nearby Monongah.
intro: Idamay sits just outside Monongah, close enough that its mineral title history follows a similar pattern: small parcels sold off from company-town land, mineral estates severed from the surface, and estates that were rarely formally probated as ownership passed down. The community itself is unincorporated, but the deed records for tracts here run through the same Marion County Courthouse books as the rest of the county.

sections.heading: Coal-camp era severances
paragraphs: Much of the mineral acreage around Idamay was severed from the surface when the land was still tied to coal-company ownership, decades before Marcellus drilling reached Marion County. That history means many current owners hold a mineral interest with no surface rights attached at all, inherited through family lines that moved away from the area generations ago.

sections.heading: Where Idamay sits relative to current drilling
paragraphs: Idamay is close to both legacy Big Injun and Gordon sand wellbores and to the newer Marcellus development running along the Route 250 corridor toward Fairmont. Whether a specific tract here is currently under lease, held by an older flat-rate arrangement, or unleased entirely depends on the individual deed and lease history — there's enough variation within a few square miles that it's worth checking your specific parcel rather than assuming based on a neighbor's situation.

sections.heading: Confirming lease status before you decide
paragraphs: Because Idamay's parcels are small and the community unincorporated, some owners have simply never checked whether a tract carries an active lease, an expired one, or none at all. A tax ticket cross-reference against the Marion County deed record settles that question directly, and it's the same step we walk through before making an offer on a fractional interest here.

If your tract sits within a mile or two of an active Route 250 corridor unit, it's also worth asking your operator directly whether a pooling amendment has been filed that would bring your acreage into a newer unit — that kind of change doesn't always reach a mineral owner's mailbox before it shows up in the courthouse record.

faqs.question: Is Idamay part of Monongah for title purposes?
faqs.answer: No — Idamay is its own unincorporated community, but records for tracts here are filed at the same Marion County Courthouse in Fairmont, and the ownership history follows a similar coal-camp severance pattern.

faqs.question: My Idamay interest has never had a royalty check — is it worth anything?
faqs.answer: Possibly, depending on whether the tract is under an active lease, held by production, or unleased. A courthouse records check confirms the lease status and any producing wellbores affecting the acreage.

faqs.question: Can I sell my share of an old family interest even if other heirs haven't been located?
faqs.answer: Yes, we buy individual fractional interests directly from heirs who can document their share, without requiring every relative to participate.

faqs.question: Does the small size of Idamay affect how a buyer values my interest?
faqs.answer: Not directly — value depends on lease terms, unit participation, and production status, not the size of the surrounding community.
